complexity.notes: The signature is a bounded computed signature (26 counters over lowercase letters with bounded word length), so adversarial hash-collision degradation does not apply and the worst case stays linear. Inefficiency: word_tuple is computed twice per word (once building the dict, once appending); a single pass with collections.defaultdict(list) would halve the signature work. The annotation 'tuple(int)' is not valid typing syntax — 'tuple[int, ...]' was intended.
complexity.summary: Each word is mapped to a 26-element character-count tuple used as a dictionary key; words sharing a signature are appended to the same list. Word length is bounded (≤100 per constraints, 3-8 per scaling note), so each signature costs O(1) effectively and total work is O(n).
